target.title: RFC: add local adaptive-refresh replay tooling
target.body:
## Decision requested

Should CodexBar upstream own an offline CLI for comparing refresh policies against a caller-supplied JSONL trace?

`AdaptiveReplayCLI` is the only new product. Its supporting targets are package-internal. This PR does not make Adaptive the default or add a production signal. It remains an RFC because `VISION.md` requires owner sign-off for a new tool and its maintenance cost.

Refs #1739 and #1861.

## Scope after review

The first revision mixed offline analysis with runtime collection. That runtime scope is gone. This PR has no app recorder, trace writer, transcript scanning, provider calls, network path, or diagnostic storage lifecycle. It also removes the unrelated Keychain test change from the earlier branch.

The current three-way diff is 27 files and +3,101/-146. Tests account for 1,387 additions. The only production source change is a smaller `AdaptiveRefreshPolicy` adapter: +9/-44 in one file, with no scheduler, setting, provider, or policy-table change.

The JSONL parser also handles Swift CRLF graphemes with `Character.isNewline`. Strict and tolerant multi-record regressions cover the two Copilot findings.

## Shared policy architecture

The previous replay baseline copied the production policy table. This revision removes that second implementation.

Dependency direction:

- `CodexBar -> AdaptiveRefreshCore`
- `AdaptiveReplayCLI -> AdaptiveReplayKit -> AdaptiveRefreshCore`

`AdaptiveRefreshPolicyCore` is package-internal and Foundation-only. It is the only type that contains the adaptive thresholds, delays, precedence, and reason codes. The app adapter maps `ProcessInfo.ThermalState`; the replay adapter maps `ReplayThermalState` and converts the result for reporting.

`MirroredAdaptivePolicy` and its parity test are deleted. Coverage now follows ownership:

- core tests cover every table boundary, constrained-state precedence, future timestamps, the 2-30 minute bounds, and the five-minute heuristic interval;
- app adapter tests cover Darwin thermal-state normalization, timestamp forwarding, and nil history;
- replay adapter tests cover replay thermal-state normalization, output conversion, and interaction advances.

The scheduler integration, setting defaults, and provider behavior are unchanged.

## Fixed policy input contract

`--policy` accepts only the seven names listed by `--help`. The earlier generic `fixed-<N>m` parser is gone, so zero, negative, unlisted, and overflowing interval strings are rejected before the trace is read or a `FixedIntervalPolicy` is constructed. The error prints the accepted names and exits nonzero.

## Data boundary

The CLI reads an explicit trace path and writes a report to stdout. Optional activity fields are input-only. No trace or fixture is committed. Runtime capture and its privacy/lifecycle contract remain out of scope.

## Author-run replay evidence

Exact head: `41c6c0dc489c0e8b45f5060796ceb1d648c70c75`

The local input has 1,780 records and SHA-256 `b1e4aa33180b7c177293eb9ed16b45e24e026d259600fba2b1b67b931b904f0b`. The raw trace remains local.

| Policy | Simulated refreshes | Per observed 24h | Simulated advances | Unconstrained active over 5m | Menu staleness p50 / p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Current Adaptive | 694 | 143.47 | 53 | 4 / 145 | 142s / 1093s |
| Activity-cap candidate | 696 | 143.88 | 53 | 0 / 145 | 139s / 1093s |
| Fixed 5m | 1,383 | 285.90 | 0 | 0 / 99 | 150s / 281s |

The shared-core and policy-name validation revisions produce the same replay result as the previous head. The run found 28 observed segments and excluded 26.10 hours with a five-minute legacy-gap heuristic. Activity fields were present for 462 of 733 decisions; 185 samples were inside the five-minute active window. The trace contains 46 recorded advances and zero timer-advance evaluations.

On this input, current Adaptive schedules 49.8% fewer simulated refreshes than fixed five minutes. The activity candidate adds two refreshes and removes four active-delay violations, but neither Adaptive variant improves p95 staleness. This does not support a default or production-policy change.

## Validation

For exact head `41c6c0dc`:

- 67 Adaptive replay/core tests passed across 8 suites.
- 3 CLI argument tests passed across 12 cases: all seven accepted names plus zero, negative, unlisted, and overflowing fixed intervals.
- 4 macOS app-adapter tests passed.
- `swift build --product AdaptiveReplayCLI` passed.
- `swift run AdaptiveReplayCLI <hash-pinned-trace>` produced the table above.
- Four real CLI invocations for the invalid fixed intervals exited 1 and printed the accepted names.
- `make check` passed: SwiftFormat 0/1,376 and SwiftLint 0 violations in 1,375 files.
- `git diff --check` passed.

An earlier head showed two red checks from one unrelated failure. The existing Kimi timing test measured 0.25113839 seconds against a strict `<0.250` assertion; the second red check was the aggregate gate reporting that shard failure. This PR does not change Kimi source or tests. GitHub CI is running the exact head above.

## Limitations

- The replay evidence comes from one machine and the raw trace is not public.
- Gap segmentation is heuristic and cannot identify sleep, reboot, a long refresh, or an event-loop stall.
- The trace predates evaluation records, so accepted versus rejected live evaluations cannot be audited.
- The result does not measure battery use, elapsed user time, provider requests, or cost.
- Both Adaptive variants have worse p95 menu staleness than fixed five minutes on this trace.

The remaining decision is product ownership: should this repository maintain the offline CLI and its package-internal analysis targets?

target.title: Add Factory/Droid API-key usage auth
target.body:
## Summary
- Add Droid usage source modes `Auto | API key | Browser cookies`, with Settings API key field and `codexbar config set-api-key --provider factory` / `FACTORY_API_KEY` / optional `~/.factory/.env` resolution.
- Reuse the existing Factory bearer billing-limits path for API keys; Auto prefers API when a key is available and falls back to cookies/WorkOS on missing/unauthorized credentials.
- Preserve API-host 401/403 across app-host fallback retries so Auto web fallback is not masked by later 404 noise.
- Unify `FactoryStatusProbeError` cases for Linux CLI builds (ubuntu CI) and rename `FactoryApi*` → `FactoryAPI*` to match repo naming.

## Deliberate notes
- **Source modes:** Factory previously advertised `[.auto, .cli]` while only implementing a web strategy. This PR switches to `[.auto, .api, .web]` and **keeps `.cli` as an Auto compatibility alias** so persisted `source: cli` configs keep validating / dispatching (Settings UI still normalizes to Auto).
- **Linux:** API-key bearer HTTP works on Linux CLI; browser-cookie/WorkOS remains macOS-only. Auto/cli skips the Linux web gate when a Factory API key is resolvable.
- **Docs:** `docs/factory.md` corrects the subscription usage endpoint from POST to GET to match the probe.

## Fork / prior review
- Fork PR (reviews already addressed): https://github.com/araa47/CodexBar/pull/1
- Rebased onto latest `steipete/CodexBar` main before opening this PR.

## Test plan
- [x] `make check`
- [x] `swift test --filter 'FactoryAPI|FactorySettingsReader|applies API key override for factory|factory config'`
- [x] CLI smoke: `CodexBarCLI usage --provider factory --source api` with `FACTORY_API_KEY`
- [x] CLI smoke: `usage --provider factory --source web` without forcing API key
- [x] Local `CodexBar.app` packaged/launched; Settings UI (Usage source + API key) checked
- [x] Codex gpt-5.6-sol + Claude fable review findings addressed (Linux enum + API casing, 401/403 host fallback)
- [ ] CI `build-linux-cli` on this PR

target.title: Fix unknown Codex model attribution
target.body:
## Summary

- Stop assigning model-less Codex token events to `gpt-5`.
- Prefer the model carried by a token event over stale `turn_context` state.
- Trim model evidence and ignore blank strings before falling through to another model field or context.
- Keep unresolved usage under an `unknown` key, rendered as `Unknown model`, without applying GPT-5 pricing.
- Rebuild the Codex cost cache as `codex-v9.json` so existing false attribution is removed.

Refs #1013. This is a follow-up to #1014: that patch recovered model state from oversized `turn_context` rows, while this patch removes the remaining assumption that an unresolved model must be GPT-5.

## Evidence

### Before

CodexBar briefly showed 211M tokens and $34.90 attributed to `gpt-5`:

![CodexBar cost history showing a false GPT-5 attribution](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/86edce19-2f46-46ce-aed3-1e45abd3efce)

The underlying Codex data for that day contained no `model:"gpt-5"` records. The local session JSONL contained 112 `gpt-5.6-sol` model records and 352 `codex-auto-review` records; `logs_2.sqlite` also contained no GPT-5 completion. A later cache refresh removed the GPT-5 row, confirming that this was transient scanner attribution rather than a backend model fallback.

The remaining cause was the scanner's final fallback:

```swift
currentModel ?? eventModel ?? "gpt-5"
```

That fallback turned missing evidence into a specific model and a priced cost. This patch keeps the usage visible but explicitly unattributed. It also restores the intended precedence for a model supplied directly by the token event.

### After: real cache rebuild

The same Jul 11 history after rebuilding with the patched scanner has no GPT-5 row. The resolved usage is attributed to `gpt-5.6-sol` and `codex-auto-review`:

![CodexBar cost history after rebuilding without the false GPT-5 row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7742809d-2a14-461c-9a15-728f51765108)

### After: unresolved-model path

I also ran the freshly built `CodexBarCLI cost` against an isolated Codex home containing one model-less `token_count` event with 55M tokens. This exercises the complete JSONL scanner, cache, pricing, and JSON output path without reading a real account:

```json
{
  "date": "2026-07-11",
  "modelBreakdowns": [
    {
      "modelName": "unknown",
      "totalTokens": 55000000
    }
  ],
  "modelsUsed": ["unknown"],
  "totalTokens": 55000000
}
```

There is no `cost` or `totalCost` field for the unknown breakdown, and no GPT-5 row. The fixture used a redacted project path and no credentials, endpoints, browser data, or Keychain access.

## Validation

- `make check`
- `DYLD_FRAMEWORK_PATH="$PWD/.build/out/Products/Debug" swift test --filter CostUsageScannerBreakdownTests --filter CostUsageCacheTests` (65 tests passed)
- `DYLD_FRAMEWORK_PATH="$PWD/.build/out/Products/Debug" swift test --filter UsageFormatterTests` (42 tests passed)

The full sharded suite reached an unrelated order-sensitive Claude test group that failed in the combined run and passed when rerun by itself. The Codex scanner/cache and formatter suites pass cleanly.
